This includes extra resolver fields that will be rejected or discarded: those raw records must not be handed to a replacement global guard on either the success or refusal path. Unexpected binding fields still fail before host preparation, and the resolver's records are not frozen or mutated.  The public `executeAuthorizedAccessCell` runner snapshots its optional caller signal once and rechecks cancellation after preflight awaits and deadline/signal composition. Supported inputs are genuine native AbortSignals and normal subclasses with their own native data state and no Proxy anywhere in the prototype chain; public `.aborted` values or getters cannot hide cancellation. Proxy signals, objects inheriting from proxies or other signals, and malformed or accessor-backed native state fail closed as `invalid_abort_signal` before inspection, credential resolution, reservation or provider dispatch. The fixed `runAccessPreflight` matrix carries one captured signal through its billable cells. The runner also passes its validated signal to OpenRouter adapter preparation, which rechecks it across credential, clock and host-preparation boundaries; direct callers may omit this preparation signal, and it is never forwarded to credential or host preparation payloads. Deadline checks run after signal composition and again after callback-capable accessors immediately before reservation or host dispatch, so elapsed synchronous work cannot start an expired operation or leave a new hold. The OpenRouter adapter copies credential response fields, binding and evidence before validation and uses only that validated snapshot across later clock callbacks. A cancellation, invalid signal or expired deadline before reservation returns a sanitized blocked/failed row with no financial hold and no reservation or provider dispatch. Once reservation begins, the existing metering state machine remains responsible for releasing a confirmed pre-dispatch hold or retaining an uncertain in-flight hold for reconciliation.
